title: Roadmap prioritization matrix for latency-cost tradeoffs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: establish a repeatable, engineering-friendly prioritization framework that augments RICE with explicit cost and latency impact signals so PM/Eng/Design can rank roadmap candidates that trade economic unit cost vs user-perceived latency. Outcome: an operational scoring sheet, sample scored initiatives covering Hosted API + Dedicated, and integration of the metric into quarterly OKR planning.
proposal: Introduce 'RICE-LC' (Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort with Latency and Cost modifiers). Rationale: vanilla RICE hides operational economics — two initiatives with similar RICE scores can have vastly different run costs or latency consequences for production. RICE-LC preserves the familiar R/I/C/E inputs while making cost and latency first-class modifiers that change priority when economics or SLOs are at stake.
scoring_rubric: Reach (R): # of unique requests/users impacted per day. Use estimated monthly active callers normalized to a 0-100 scale. Example: 10k daily callers -> normalize to 10
Impact (I): measurable end-user benefit per affected request. 0.25 (minor) | 1 (noticeable) | 2 (major) | 3 (transformational). Keep continuous values for nuance.
Confidence (C): percent confidence in estimates (0-100). Use 25/50/75/90 buckets with justification.
Effort (E): engineering effort in story points (or weeks). Enter numeric points; lower is better (denominator).

Cost Modifier (CM): expected change to per-token or per-request unit cost. Express as multiplier >0. Example: CM=1.2 means 20% higher unit cost; CM=0.8 means 20% savings. Use +/− expected delta versus baseline. Guidance: separate one-time infra cost vs incremental per-request cost in comments.

Latency Penalty (LP): expected effect on 95th P99 latency in ms. Convert to a penalty multiplier using a lookup table: 0-5ms -> 1.0, 6-25ms -> 0.9, 26-75ms -> 0.7, >75ms -> 0.4. If initiative reduces latency, use >1.0 (e.g., 1.2). This ensures improvements can boost priority even if cost increases slightly.
Formula: RawRICE = (R * I * (C/100)) / E. FinalScore = RawRICE * (1/CM) * LP. Interpret: higher FinalScore => higher priority. This penalizes expensive initiatives and rewards latency-reducing work.
Normalization: after computing FinalScore for the candidate set, normalize to 0-100 for presentation on roadmap dashboards and OKR planning.

Edge cases: security/compliance work can bypass CM/LP modifiers and be promoted based on 'must-have' labels. Also include non-linear caps for CM to avoid amplifying tiny CM changes into big rank flips.
examples: Example A - Autoscale Dedicated GPU pools: R=6 (targets 60k/day), I=2 (reduces retries for heavy customers), C=60, E=40 points, CM=1.15 (expected 15% higher baseline cost due to warm pools), LP=1.2 (reduces P95 by ~40ms). RawRICE=(6*2*0.6)/40=0.18. FinalScore=0.18*(1/1.15)*1.2=0.188 => normalized ~29/100 in current candidate set.

Example B - KV prefix caching improvement: R=12, I=1.5, C=80, E=8 points, CM=0.85 (saves 15% per token), LP=1.0 (negligible latency change for P95). RawRICE=(12*1.5*0.8)/8=1.8. FinalScore=1.8*(1/0.85)*1.0=2.118 => normalized ~72/100. In this simplified comparison, caching ranks higher due to strong reach and cost savings despite modest impact per request.

Interpretation: the framework surfaces that some medium-impact, low-effort cost-savers should be prioritized ahead of high-effort infra projects unless latency SLOs are the highest priority and tied to OKRs.
decision_log: 2026-03-10 - Proposal drafted by Aisha Patel. Rationale and formula reviewed with Miguel Santos and Priya Rao (Eng).

2026-03-11 - Engineering feedback: requested clearer guidance for CM inputs (separate fixed vs variable cost) and an automated calculator in the roadmap spreadsheet. Action: Miguel to produce a Google Sheet template (PRD link in attachments).

2026-03-12 - PM/Eng sync: agreed to pilot RICE-LC on next cycle's candidate set (10 initiatives). Also agreed that security/compliance flagged initiatives are 'must-pass' and excluded from CM/LP demotion.
comments: 2026-03-10 Miguel Santos: 'I like the LP lookup table; suggest we make the cutpoints configurable per product (Hosted vs Dedicated have different latency sensitivity).'
2026-03-11 Priya Rao: 'Engineering will provide rough cost deltas by 2026-03-15. For Dedicated, CM needs to factor reserved capacity amortization. I'll add estimates to the sheet.'
2026-03-12 Daniel Kim (Design): 'If we surface normalized FinalScore in the Console roadmap UI, include a tooltip explaining CM/LP so non-technical stakeholders understand cost tradeoffs.'

2026-03-12 Aisha Patel: 'Next steps: (1) Miguel creates sheet template and automation; (2) PMs score 10 candidate initiatives by 2026-03-18; (3) Review scoring in Roadmap Planning session 2026-03-19.'
